practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 1: Under the Charter Act of 1793, the salaries and allowances of the members and staff of the Board of Control were to be paid out of which of the following?
opts: British Treasury
Indian Revenues
Consolidated Fund of Great Britain
Private trade duties of Company servants
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 1: The Charter Act of 1793 laid down that the salaries and expenses of the members of the Board of Control and their staff were to be paid out of the Indian revenues. This became a major point of criticism by early Indian nationalists, who termed it a part of the 'Drain of Wealth'.

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 2: How did the Charter Act of 1793 affect the overriding power originally given to Lord Cornwallis?
opts: It abolished the overriding power entirely.
It restricted the overriding power to military matters only.
It extended the overriding power to all future Governors-General and Governors of Presidencies.
It limited the overriding power to the Presidency of Bengal only.
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 2: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the overriding power given to Lord Cornwallis over his council to all future Governors-General and Governors of the Presidencies (Bombay and Madras).

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 3: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Commander-in-Chief's position under the Charter Act of 1793?
opts: He was automatically the ex-officio member of the Governor-General's Council.
He was not to be a member of the Governor-General's Council unless specially appointed.
He was made the head of the civil executive government.
His office was completely separated from the military command.
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 3: The Charter Act of 1793 provided that the Commander-in-Chief was not to be a member of the Governor-General's Council unless he was specially appointed to it by the Court of Directors.

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 4: What was the statutory financial payment the East India Company was required to make annually to the British Government under the 1793 Act?
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 4: The Charter Act of 1793 required the East India Company to pay a fixed sum of £500,000 annually to the British Government from its surplus Indian revenues.

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 5: Which of the following is a key feature introduced by the Charter Act of 1793?
opts: It extended the trade monopoly of the East India Company for another 20 years.
It abolished the trade monopoly of the East India Company.
It established the Board of Control in London.
It allowed Christian missionaries to enter India.
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 5: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the trade monopoly of the East India Company for an additional period of 20 years. Trade monopoly was abolished later by the Charter Act of 1813 (except for tea and China trade), while Christian missionaries were allowed in 1813. The Board of Control was established in 1784.

mockTestQuestions.q: Mock Question 51: The Charter Act of 1793 consolidated the separation of revenue administration from judicial functions. This resulted in the disappearance of which of the following courts?
opts: Sadar Diwani Adalat
Sadar Nizamat Adalat
Maal Adalats (Revenue Courts)
Supreme Court of Calcutta
mockTestQuestions.sol: Explanation for Mock Question 51: The Charter Act of 1793 separated the revenue administration from the judicial functions, which led to the disappearance of the Maal Adalats (revenue courts) in Bengal, transferring their cases to the civil courts (Diwani Adalats).

mockTestQuestions.q: Mock Question 52: Which of the following Acts first laid down the principle that the Board of Control members and staff are paid out of Indian revenues?
opts: Regulating Act of 1773
Pitt's India Act of 1784
Amending Act of 1786
Charter Act of 1793
mockTestQuestions.sol: Explanation for Mock Question 52: The principle of paying the Board of Control members and staff out of the Indian revenues was introduced by the Charter Act of 1793. This was a significant feature that institutionalized the drain of wealth from India to Britain.
